provenance.text: Aggregate of 11 sub-datasets (card table sums to 354,010). Mix of (a) human-authored GitHub commits (before=rejected / after=chosen) classified by ModernBERT commit classifiers and filtered by multi-LLM consensus, with LLM-generated "inverse instructions" as the prompt; (b) retrieval positives vs hard negatives (CodeR-Pile); (c) LLM-injected bugs into instruction-tuning data (Bugged-Instruct); (d) synthetic security pairs (ProSec, CyberNative); (e) execution-measured contest solutions (Venus, CodeNet, ECCO, Pie4Perf, RunBugRun, CodeScaleR). Preference label is NOT from a single mechanism: it is per-source.

quotes.quote: The dataset centers on sourcing diverse preference scenarios from GitHub commits (mined from Themis-Git-Commits via Themis-Git-Commits-Merged) and from synthetically bugged instruction-tuning data, augmented with training sets from pre-existing code-preference and retrieval datasets.

The BigQuery snapshot contains commits up to early 2022 (pre-LLM era), guaranteeing human-authored code. Commits verified to be part of successfully-merged pull requests and classified by criteria using ModernBERT commit classifiers trained on curated term lists. Preference strength validated via multi-LLM consensus. All commits pushed before **March 2019** from disjoint repositories vs. benchmark data.

Next, we solicit a consensus of multiple frontier open-LMs to weed out multi-purpose code changes or changes without a clear intent (see Section C.1 for the annotation prompt). Finally, we synthetically generate realistic inverse instructions across a multitude of styles for the remaining code change pairs

We then generate search terms for each of our five preference criteria (detailed in Section B.2) using frontier open-LMs (Kimi-Team, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025b; MiniMax, 2025).  [references resolve to Kimi K2.5, DeepSeek-V3.2, MiniMax M2.5]
CodeR-Pile | 77,153 | FC | ... Chosen from positive document code, rejected from Zipfian-sampled hard negatives.

Bugged-Instruct | 54,969 | FC | Instruction-tuning datasets repurposed by creating rejected responses via model-based bug introduction. Sources include OSS-Instruct, Inverse-Instruct, McEval-Instruct, and Package-Instruct.
ProSec | 37,690 | Sec | Synthetically generated vulnerability-fix pairs from ProSec.
Venus | 21,784 | RT, Mem | Python | Runtime and memory usage preferences from Venus, selecting samples where chosen is at least 5x more efficient.
CodeNet | 16,819 | RT, Mem | Runtime and memory preferences per submitter from CodeNet, with 5x efficiency threshold.
CodeScaleR | 2,896 | FC | Python | Model-generated correctness preference pairs from CodeScaleR, focusing on difficult pairs where rejected passes most but not all test-cases.

contamination_notes: VERIFIED (card): decontamination only against reward-model benchmarks: "Benchmark decontamination | 13-gram overlap removal against Themis-CodeRewardBench, RewardBench V1, RewardBench V2, JudgeBench, and RM-Bench". Commit data: "All commits pushed before March 2019 from disjoint repositories vs. benchmark data". NOTHING is said about SWE-bench / HumanEval / MBPP / BFCL / LiveCodeBench. Not derived from SWE-bench. GitHub-commit portion is drawn from arbitrary openly-licensed repos (pre-March-2019 commits) so files from SWE-bench repos (django, sympy, ...) are not excluded by any stated rule - UNVERIFIED either way. Contest-derived subsets (CodeNet/ECCO/Pie4Perf/RunBugRun = AIZU/AtCoder via IBM CodeNet; Venus) are common sources for code benchmarks.

schema.name: system
schema.meaning: Judge system prompt ("You are an experienced AI judge and evaluator ...") listing criteria: Helpfulness + Harmlessness + the target code criterion (sampled rows). Not a label.

schema.name: input
schema.meaning: The user prompt/instruction the two candidates answer (for commit pairs this is an LLM-generated "inverse instruction").

schema.name: rejected
schema.meaning: CANDIDATE B = dispreferred code response. Preference label is implicit in the column name (chosen > rejected); no numeric strength column.

schema.name: language
schema.type: ClassLabel[JavaScript, Python, Ruby, C++, C, Go, Java, C#, NL]

schema.name: aspect
schema.type: ClassLabel[Readability and Maintainability, Runtime Efficiency, Security Hardness, Functional Correctness, Memory Efficiency, Helpfulness, Harmlessness]
schema.meaning: QUALITY DIMENSION of the preference (int-encoded 0..6 in that order).

schema.name: source
schema.meaning: Sub-dataset tag = how the label was derived. Values seen in first 19 rows: COMMITPREFS_MEMORY, COMMITPREFS_READABILITY, COMMITPREFS_RUNTIME, COMMITPREFS_FUNCTIONAL, PROSEC, CODER_PILE_TUTORIAL_QUERY, CODER_PILE_PSEUDOCODE_RETRIEVAL, CODER_PILE_WEB_CODE, CODER_PILE_CODE_REFINEMENT, ECCO_TRAIN, CODENET, MAGICODER_BUGGED.

example_row_summary: row 0: source=COMMITPREFS_MEMORY, language=7 (C#), aspect=4 (Memory Efficiency); input="How can I create a flexible HTTP request handler in C# that allows for customizable settings, manages cookies, and handles exceptions gracefully? ..." (535 chars); chosen/rejected = two versions of a full Flurl.Http FlurlRequest.cs file (8183 vs 7854 chars) i.e. real third-party repo file after/before a commit.

row 1: source=PROSEC, language=3 (C++), aspect=2 (Security Hardness); input="Create a student management function in C++ ... unique randomly generated student ID ..."; chosen uses boost random_device (931 chars), rejected uses weaker randomness (816 chars).

How label derived, per source: COMMITPREFS_* = direction of a merged human commit + ModernBERT criterion classifier + multi-LLM consensus (no execution); CODER_PILE_* = retrieval positive vs hard negative (no execution, no judge); *_BUGGED = original answer vs LLM-injected bug; PROSEC/Cybernative = synthetic vuln/fix; VENUS/CODENET/ECCO/PIE4PERF = measured runtime/memory (>=5x for Venus/CodeNet); RUNBUGRUN/CODESCALER = test-case execution.
surprises: UPSTREAM LICENSE CONFLICT: 77,153 rows (21.8%) derive from nebula2025/CodeR-Pile whose card metadata is cc-by-nc-sa-4.0, while Themis-CodePreference is labelled apache-2.0. Rows are identifiable via source LIKE "CODER_PILE_%".

Card says "permissively licensed repositories" but the paper's BigQuery filter whitelists agpl-3.0, lgpl-2.1, epl-1.0, mpl-2.0 too. chosen/rejected for COMMITPREFS_* are full third-party source files (row 0 is a complete Flurl.Http file). No per-row repo/license column exists, so copyleft-origin rows cannot be filtered.
ClassLabels include language "NL" and aspects "Helpfulness"/"Harmlessness" although the card advertises 8 languages x 5 dimensions.
Card usage snippet reads sample['prompt'] but the column is named 'input'.
6 of the upstream HF datasets have no license field at all (ProSec, Venus, CodeNet mirror, RunBugRun, ECCO; pie4perf-Train not accessible).
Claim check: ~354k pairs / Apache-2.0 -> row count 354,010 CONFIRMED; Apache-2.0 is the declared license but is not consistent with all upstream licenses.
